as_told.title: Luis Alvarez's asteroid impact theory of the dinosaur extinction

plain: This is the story of how the dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago, and of the scientists who first said why. The writer Graham Hancock says on Jesse Michels' podcast that nobody now disputes that a comet or asteroid did it, and that the proof is the Chicxulub crater, buried deep under land and sea around Mexico's Yucatan, which in another telling he places under the Gulf of Mexico. He credits the scientists Luis and Walter Alvarez, who put the idea forward in the 1980s, and says it was not accepted until the crater was found. Michels himself tells it more briefly, crediting only Luis Alvarez. They tell it as an example of an idea that was rejected at first and later proven right.
